sentences.text:
Court No. - 76
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 106 of 2024
Applicant :- Shahzad Ali And Another
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
1. Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicants is taken on record.

2. The instant anticipatory bail application put up before this Court today by the order passed by
Hon'ble Acting Chief Justice dated 16.1.2024.

3.Heard Sri Mohd. Sakir, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Jhamman Ram, , learned Aga-I for
the State.

4. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants in F.I.R./Case
Crime No.173 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 379, 411, 120-B Ipc and Section 4/21 of
Mines and Mineral (Development & Regulation) Act, 1957 as well as Section 3 of P.P. Act, Police
Station-Shivala Kala, District-Bijnor, with a prayer to enlarge them on anticipatory bail during trial.
5.

At the very outset, learned counsel for the applicants submits that he does not want to press the instant anticipatory bail application on merit and a direction may be given to the court concerned Shahzad Ali And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180984098/
1 that if applicants appear before it and apply for bail then the bail application shall be dispose off in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Breau of Investigation and another (2022) 10 SCC 51.
6. Learned AGA is not having any objection if any such direction is given to the court concerned.
7. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.
8.

sentences.text: Considering the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the applicants and learned AGA, in case applicants appear before the court concerned within two weeks from today and apply for bail in the instant matter, then their bail application shall be disposed off by the court concerned in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil (supra).
9. The instant anticipatory bail application stands disposed off accordingly.
